newsitem.title: UK: Barclays squeezed higher in stock shortage.
newsitem.headline: Barclays squeezed higher in stock shortage.

text.p: Banking group Barclays Plc romped higher on Thursday as investors scrambled to increase their weighting in the expanding bank sector ahead of further building society flotations later this year, dealers said.

With Alliance & Leicester Plc rising for a second day after its storming flotation this week, dealers said investors may have been spooked into pushing extra cash into the sector ahead of the Halifax and Woolwich floats later this year.
A shortage of Barclays shares in the market exaggerated the gains, sending the stock up 50-1/2p or 4.8 percent to 11.09 stg by 1351 GMT, in active trade of 6.3 million shares.
"You have got to get your weightings up for the building societies coming in and the way to do it is to buy other banks," said one senior dealer.
He pointed out Barclays was up more sharply than other leading banks since it had dropped sharply from its record 1234-1/2 stg in mid February.
Lloyds TSB Group Plc by contrast was up 13p at 550 in volume of 10.8 million, after earlier setting a record 555-1/2p.
Among other banks HSBC Holdings Plc was up 26p at 15.82 stg and National Westminster Bank Plc was up 15-1/2p at 716-1/2.
Earlier Bank of Scotland Plc, up 21p or 6.2 percent at 359-1/2, stoked gains in the sector after Wednesday's well-recieved results.
"There has been a bit of a squeeze," said one market-maker, "all the banks have gone ballistic but Barclays is the one they have really chased."
